clue.text: Happy nobody sees work of Coward

parts.note: happy means carefree and cheerful, an old literary sense
a ghost or phantom is something nobody can see

explanation.surface: A cheerful person who sees nobody is a typical character in a Noel Coward play.
explanation.walkthrough: Noel Coward was an English playwright; his comedy about a ghostly first wife is the work meant. 'Nobody sees' describes an invisible being.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic play about a medium and a returning ghost is one of Noel Coward's best-known stage pieces.

clue.text: Fish band-leader catches by stream

indicators.note: the leader of the word band is its opening letter

parts.note: a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A bandleader catches fish beside a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band-leader' looks like a conductor, but it is only the first letter of 'band'; 'catches by' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatfish of European waters related to the turbot goes by this name.

clue.text: Unfortunate one Conservative has it disallowed

parts.note: unfortunate, as in an ill turn of events
the Roman numeral for one
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: An unlucky Tory politician finds something banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disallowed is forbidden by law or rules, hence unlawful.

clue.text: Tight currency needed to qualify for honours list

definitions.text: needed to qualify for honours list

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is high
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Sound money and tight finances are needed before anyone gets on the honours list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests a squeeze on money beside 'currency', but it means intoxicated. An honours list here is a list of top exam results.
explanation.definitionFit: Top scores in an exam are what place a student among those graded with distinction.

clue.text: See 1
Next month you start to substitute

parts.note: prox, short for proximo, is old commercial shorthand for next month

indicators.note: the start of the word you is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Next month you begin as a stand-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A proxy is a person authorised to act or vote in another's place.

clue.text: Acknowledgment of pet Eric tormented

indicators.note: tormented suggests something twisted about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eric's pet suffers, and someone acknowledges it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tormented' rearranges the letters of PET ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A written slip confirming payment or delivery is a formal acknowledgment.

clue.text: Agency girl puts lock an siren

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker sent by an employment agency
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An office temp puts a lock on a siren.
explanation.walkthrough: A temp is the classic office worker supplied by an agency; 'puts ... on' places the lock after her.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman who lures men, as does an enchantress.

clue.text: Misfortune running into attendant sacking

indicators.note: running into puts one piece inside the other, as one thing enters another

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
ill means trouble or misfortune

explanation.surface: Bad luck befalls an attendant who is fired from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' looks like dismissal from a job, but here it means plundering a captured town; 'running into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking a town means plundering it, looting by force.

clue.text: Fool giving navigator set of teeth

parts.note: the cox steers a rowing boat
a comb is a row of teeth

explanation.surface: A fool gives a rower a set of false teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: A comb's tines are its teeth, so a comb is a set of teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, conceited man, a dandy, originally the jester's cap.

clue.text: Rare In have inferior twisted

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Rare In have inferior twisted' is garbled: 'In have' supplies nothing in UNDER (inferior) + DONE (twisted), and the original wording could not be found.

clue.text: Second or third reward

parts.note: a racing bet that pays when the horse comes second or third rather than winning

explanation.surface: A prize for coming second or third.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a wager placed to finish in the top places pays out on a second or third.

clue.text: Small letter from abroad

parts.note: reads as a short note from overseas, but means a tiny Greek character

explanation.surface: A brief note from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The ninth letter of the Greek alphabet is also a word for a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's smallest character, also a byword for a very small amount.

clue.text: Parent responsible for strike on the Queen Elizabeth

parts.note: to pat is to strike lightly
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A father responsible for a strike aboard the ocean liner Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen Elizabeth looks like the liner, but it gives the monarch's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, used in old-fashioned British slang.

clue.text: Full-time scoundrel daughter put off temporarily

parts.note: a pro is a full-time professional
a rogue is a scoundrel
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: At full time a rogue's daughter was postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is suspended without dissolution when its session is ended, a temporary discontinuance.

clue.text: Boat race crew even has majority

parts.note: the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race is rowed by crews of eight
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A boat race crew has an even majority.
explanation.walkthrough: Majority here is the age of coming of age in law, traditionally twenty-one but now this in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal age of adulthood in the UK, when one attains one's majority, is this many years.

clue.text: Heavens! Some predicament in store for odds and ends

parts.note: Glory! is an exclamation of surprise, like Heavens!
a hole is a fix or predicament

explanation.surface: Someone cries out at a predicament they find in a storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage this is an untidy cupboard or room where junk is stuffed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard or drawer where miscellaneous junk is thrown is called this in Britain.

clue.text: Study female second hand troubled

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
used goods are secondhand

explanation.surface: A student is troubled by a secondhand woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being troubled and muddled in mind is a state of bewilderment.

clue.text: Fresh start to holiday by guest at banquet

indicators.note: the start of the word Fresh is its opening letter

parts.note: Easter is a spring holiday

explanation.surface: A fresh start to the holidays for a guest at the banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: One who dines at a lavish meal is someone eating at a banquet.

clue.text: Ought a small relative to have deserted refuge?

parts.note: ought, or aught, means nought, the figure O
sis is a short, small form of sister

explanation.surface: Should a younger relative have abandoned shelter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' reads as abandoned, but means found in a desert; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in the desert is a place of refuge in the sands.

clue.text: Operator of bar in Cork

definitions.meaning: one who stops or bars the way
a bung that closes a bottle

explanation.surface: A barman working in the Irish city of Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork reads as the Irish city; the capital is only there for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who halts or bars, and a bung that plugs a bottle neck.

clue.text: Man in the sea heard complainant

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is spoken and we take its sound

parts.note: a moaner is a complainer

explanation.surface: A man in the sea heard a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Mona is the Latin name for the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea; in a non-rhotic accent MOANER sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romans called the Isle of Man by this name, an island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Quarrel with what the orchestra said?

explanation.surface: An argument over what the orchestra said.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into 'band' plus an adjective ending, words of the band.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade heated remarks is to argue, and the band's speech is the pun.

clue.text: Drunk out of sight

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for heavily intoxicated, and lacking sight altogether.

clue.text: Not sound of bird

definitions.meaning: a ...-bird, child's word for a small bird

explanation.walkthrough: A 'dicky heart' is British slang for an unsound one.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for shaky or unwell, and a nursery word for a small bird.

clue.text: Brief trouble with contract

parts.note: curt means brief, abrupt
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A short trouble with a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a legal agreement but is the verb, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten or cut back is to make something smaller.

clue.text: Consolidate agreement

explanation.definitionFit: To press firmly together, and a formal pact between parties.

clue.text: The Camptown jockey's run out of ridicule

parts.note: the minstrel song Camptown Races uses 'de' for 'the' in its dialect lyrics
a jockey's run on a horse is a ride

explanation.surface: The Camptown Races jockey has run out of mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camptown Races' is an old American minstrel song whose lyrics write 'the' as 'de'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or scorn someone is to laugh at them.

clue.text: Give away money put on fish

parts.note: a bet is money staked on an outcome
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Someone gives away money staked on a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret or a person treacherously is to give them away.
